newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex 1996/97 net seen 28 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Vendex 1996/97 net seen 28 pct higher.

text.p: Analysts expect retail and business services group Vendex International NV to post a 28 percent rise in net profit in the 1996/97 year to Jan 31.
The company is due to provide an indication of its 1996/97 results on Tuesday, with fuller figures scheduled for April 15.
Forecasts of Vendex' 1996/97 net profit ranged from 451 to 589 million guilders in 1996/97, with a consensus of 531 million, compared with 415 million guilders in 1995/96.
Vendex's results are notoriously complex and some analysts prefer to focus on operating profits which are expected to rise to 466 million guilders from 412 million.

The operating profit figures include "income from the redevelopment and sale of real estate" while the net profit figures include "changes in value and income from receivables forming part of fixed assets and from securities".
Despite such complications analysts expect underlying earnings to show a clear improvement.
"Both including and excluding real estate income, profits are set to rise in all divisions," said NIBStrating analyst Nils van Elzelingen.
Dennis Jullens of ING Barings expects higher operating profits at all divisions, with interest focusing on positive news from Vendex' department stores and speciality stores.
"The increase in consumer spending will have a positive impact on results in both department stores and speciality stores," he said.
Jullens said the acquisition of OEM, which operates the Hans Anders chain of opticians and other similar stores, would also contribute to higher earnings.
Jurgen Veenker of MeesPierson saw a judicious rejuggling of the Vroom & Dreesmann department stores' product ranges and real estate assets as the driving force behind improved profits.
Profits in Vendex' services sector are also expected to show an increase, but analysts were divided over how big it would be.
Both Veenker and Van Elzelingen said operating profit in temporary employment services was likely to have increased by some 15 percent, but Jullens saw only a five percent increase.

"Outside the Netherlands, the situation wasn't very good. France showed no growth, I expect operating results to include a charge of some 10 million guilders for measures taken at (French cleaning unit) Abilis," Jullens said.
Analysts are not expecting Vendex's statement to provide any fresh details of plans to demerge the group's business services unit -- creating separately listed retail and service entities.
These plans were announced along with the acquisition of French temporary employment group BIS in January.
Jullens said he was generally optimistic about the outlook for Vendex in 1997/98.
"Consumer spending is good, the French and Belgian markets for temporary employment look better and the share price should benefit from positive sentiment triggered by the demerger plans," he said.
